subject: Does specifying "map" in RTMB's MakeADFun work?

messages.author: e97222832aa0e335
messages.subject: Does specifying "map" in RTMB's MakeADFun work?
parts:
Probably I'm doing this wrong, but I have the following very simple example for turning off estimation of specific parameters using the map function:

require(RTMB);
objfun<-function(params){
  getAll(params);
  y %~% dnorm(a[1]+a[2]*x,1);
}

a = c(1,2);
x = 0:10
y = a[1] + a[2]*x + rnorm(length(x),0,1);
plot(x,y);
params = list(a=a);
map = list(a=factor(1:length(a)));
# map$a[2] = NA;

obj = MakeADFun(objfun,parameters=params,map=map);
opt = nlminb(obj$par,obj$fn,obj$gr);
sdr = sdreport(obj);
summary(sdr)

When I run it as above (with map$a[2] = NA; commented out), for the summary I get 
   Estimate Std. Error
a 0.7388331 0.56407607
a 2.1037572 0.09534626

When I uncomment the `map$a[2] = NA;` line, I get the error 
Error in optimHess(par.fixed, obj$fn, obj$gr) :
  non-finite value supplied by optim

and the value for a[2] in opt$par (or obj$env$last.par), which should be fixed at 2 if I've done it right, is NA.

So is this a problem with me or with RTMB?

Thanks for any help!

William T. Stockhausen

messages.author: e97222832aa0e335
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Does specifying "map" in RTMB's MakeADFun work?
parts:
Thanks for your suggestions! They both worked, but they seem a bit less general than what the MakeADFun documentation suggests you can do. 

My mistake was apparently doing this:

map$a = factor(length(a)); map$a[2] = NA; (i.e., setting the NA after creating the factor)

to "fix" a[2] (which didn't work) whereas doing the following did work:

ma = 1:length(a); ma[2] = NA; map$a = factor(ma);

I.e., setting the NAs before creating the factor vector. I don't know (quite obviously) if there are other approaches, but would love to hear about them.

One thing I was a bit surprised by was that the sdreport'ed parameter values did not include the "fixed" values. However, I was able to get the "full" parameter vector after optimization (i.e., including the fixed value a[2] (with std=0)) by adding ADREPORT(a) to the objective function code.

William T. Stockhausen
